paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. God's judgments are just and true, and the singers say so before a single bowl is poured. They sing, "Great and wonderful are Your works, O Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations!" (Revelation 15:3). Later the angel of the waters and the altar say it too (Revelation 16:5-7).

Now look at the people on the receiving end. I think this part is heavy, friend, with the sores, the blood, the scorching heat and the darkness. And through it all, three times they curse God (Revelation 16:9, 11, 21). Twice the passage says they "did not repent" (Revelation 16:9, 11).

So where does that leave you and me? Right in the middle of the bowls, the passage says, "Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed, so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed." (Revelation 16:15). A thief sends no calendar invite, so I think awake and clothed is about being ready before it happens, and Jesus says the same: "Therefore keep watch, because you do not know on what day your Lord will come." (Matthew 24:42). I never guess the day, since Matthew 24:36 says only the Father knows it, so I keep my ovens warm and my cookie boxes filling for the Supper, and you keep watch and keep getting ready in the Word, friend, because Revelation 19:7 says the bride has made herself ready.
